title: Capslox Keymap Configuration
description: Schema for keymap.jsonc — the Capslox keyboard remapping configuration file.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference (ignored by the engine).

version.description: Schema version in MAJOR.MINOR format (e.g. "1.0", "2.0"). Single-digit like "2" is accepted and treated as "2.0". MAJOR must be >= 1.

custom_modifiers.description: Map of physical key name → custom modifier declaration. String shorthand: alias only (tap defaults to key name, timeout 200ms). Object form: { "alias": "cx", "tap": "esc", "timeout_ms": 300 }. Declaring a key here provides a default mod_tap fallback — no explicit mod_tap binding needed.

oneOf.description: Alias name (string shorthand). Tap defaults to key name, timeout 200ms.

tap.description: Tap action (string key syntax or action object). Defaults to the physical key name.

vars.description: User-defined variables for DRY config authoring. Each key maps a name to any JSON value. Reference with { "$ref": "/vars/<name>" } elsewhere in the config.

layers.description: Ordered list of layers. First matching binding wins (top layer first).

key_sequence_timeout_ms.description: Auto-reset key sequence state after N ms of inactivity. Omit for unlimited (Vim-style).

experimental_actions.description: Opt-in to use Alpha-tier actions (preview features) in this build. When true, the engine skips stability gating — Alpha actions stay live instead of being replaced with noop. Useful for previewing features before they ship to stable. Stable-tier actions are always available regardless of this flag.

activation.description: How this layer is activated. Defaults to "base".

on_miss.description: What happens when a key has no binding in this layer.

enabled.description: Whether this layer is active. Disabled layers are skipped.

bundle_ids.description: App bundle IDs that activate this layer (supports dot-boundary wildcards like "com.jetbrains.*").

oneOf.description: Layer automatically activated when the frontmost app matches any bundle ID.

MissBehavior.description: Behavior when a key has no binding in this layer. "continue" = check next layer, "block" = swallow the key, "pass_to_os" = send to OS.

oneOf.description: String shorthand: directive keyword or key syntax. Directives: "continue" (fall through), "block" (swallow), "pass_to_os" (send to OS). Key syntax: [modifier-]key[ [modifier-]key]... with optional *N repeat (1-999). Modifiers: ctrl, shift, alt/opt, cmd/win/meta/super, or custom. Keys: a-z, 0-9, space, enter, tab, esc, backspace, delete, caps, up/down/left/right, home/end/pageup/pagedown, f1-f20, [ ] / = , . ; ', minus, backslash, backtick, kp_0-kp_9, kp_enter/kp_plus/kp_minus/kp_multiply/kp_divide/kp_decimal/kp_equal/kp_clear. Examples: "cmd-shift-a", "left", "ctrl-[ b", "alt-left*5", "continue".

Binding.description: A binding maps a trigger key to an action. Forms: (1) string shorthand — "cmd-c", "continue", "block", "pass_to_os", "noop"; (2) action object — {"action": "send_keys", "keys": "cmd-c"}, which is sugar for {"type": "action", "action": "send_keys", ...} with the redundant "type" omitted; (3) temporal binding — {"type": "mod_tap", ...} / {"type": "long_press", ...}. The engine also accepts the explicit {"type": "action", ...} form at runtime, but the sugar form is canonical.

BindingDirectiveObject.description: Directive binding (key-level on_miss override). "continue" = fall through, "block" = swallow, "pass_to_os" = send to OS.

tap.description: Action to fire on tap (short press). The hold action activates the key as a modifier.

timeout_ms.description: Max duration (ms) for a tap vs hold decision. Default: 200.

BindingModTapObject.description: Modifier-tap: hold = use key as modifier, tap = fire action.

long.description: Action for long press (held past threshold).

threshold_ms.description: Duration (ms) before switching from short to long. Default: 500.

BindingLongPressObject.description: Long-press: different actions based on press duration.

oneOf.description: Key syntax shorthand or "noop". Key syntax: [modifier-]key[ [modifier-]key]... with optional *N repeat (1-999). Modifiers: ctrl, shift, alt/opt, cmd/win/meta/super, or custom. Keys: a-z, 0-9, space, enter, tab, esc, backspace, delete, caps, up/down/left/right, home/end/pageup/pagedown, f1-f20, [ ] / = , . ; ', minus, backslash, backtick, kp_0-kp_9, kp_enter/kp_plus/kp_minus/kp_multiply/kp_divide/kp_decimal/kp_equal/kp_clear. Examples: "left", "cmd-shift-a", "ctrl-[ b", "noop".

Action.description: An action describes WHAT to do. Can be a string shorthand or a typed object with "action" discriminator.

ActionObject.description: Any action type used directly as a binding (without an explicit Binding wrapper). Matches objects whose "action" field is an action discriminator, not a binding type.

keys.description: Key syntax string: [modifier-]key[ [modifier-]key]... with optional *N repeat (1-999). Examples: "cmd-c", "ctrl-[ b", "alt-left*5".

label.description: Optional which-key menu label (F13 M2). Object form only.

ActionSendKeysObject.description: Send a key sequence (one or more key combos with optional repeat).

actions.description: Ordered list of actions to execute sequentially.

ActionNoopObject.description: Noop: consume the key but do nothing (useful in when-clauses to disable a binding for specific apps).

oneOf.description: Multiple conditional overrides, checked in order.

WhenClauses.description: Conditional overrides: when the frontmost app matches, use a different action.

oneOf.description: Literal list of app bundle IDs (supports dot-boundary wildcards like "com.jetbrains.*").

apps.description: App bundle IDs to match. Can be a literal array or a { "$ref": "/vars/<name>" } reference.

action.description: Action to use when the frontmost app matches.

WhenClause.description: A single conditional override: when the frontmost app matches, use this action instead.

$ref.description: JSON Pointer to a value in the same document (e.g. "/vars/apps_emacs_keybindings"). Leading '#' is optional.

RefObject.description: A $ref object that references another value in the document via JSON Pointer (RFC 6901).
